sentences.zh: 中山公訓為蒲州總管，以杲為府司馬、州治中，兼知州府事。

translations.literal: Duke of Zhongshan Xun was headquarters commander of Pu Province; made Gao headquarters marshal, provincial chief administrator, concurrently overseeing provincial headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Xun became headquarters commander of Pu Province, Du Gao was made his headquarters marshal and chief administrator, with concurrent charge of provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 加使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Given added Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Protocol to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He received the added ranks of bearer of the staff of authority, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and equal in protocol to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 及華皎來附，詔令衛公直督元定等援之。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao came to submit; edict ordered Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi to supervise Yuan Ding and others to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao defected to Zhou, an edict ordered Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi to lead Yuan Ding and others to his aid.

sentences.zh: 與陳人交戰，我師不利，元定等竝沒。

translations.literal: Battling Chen people, our army unfavorable; Yuan Ding and others all lost.
translations.idiomatic: In fighting Chen, Zhou forces fared badly and Yuan Ding and his men were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 自是，連兵不息，東南騷動。

translations.literal: From this onward, continuous warfare did not cease; southeast in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: From then on fighting continued without pause and the southeast was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 高祖患之，乃授杲御正中大夫，使於陳，論保境息民之意。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoyu worried about this; thereupon granted Gao Proper Central Upper Grand Master; sent to Chen; discussed the intent of guarding borders and resting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoyu, troubled by the situation, appointed Du Gao proper central upper grand master and sent him to Chen to propose halting the border war and giving the people peace.

sentences.zh: 陳宣帝遣其黃門侍郎徐陵謂杲曰：「兩國通好，本欲救患分災，彼朝受我叛人，何也？

translations.literal: Emperor Xuandi of Chen sent his Palace Gate Gentleman Xu Ling to say to Gao: "Two states communicate good relations, originally wishing to rescue troubles and share disasters; that court receives our rebels — why?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuandi of Chen sent his palace gate gentleman Xu Ling to tell Du Gao, "Our states were allies meant to help each other in hardship — why does your court shelter our deserters?

sentences.zh: 」杲答曰：「陳主昔在本朝，非慕義而至，上授以柱國，位極人臣，子女玉帛，備禮將送，遂主社稷，孰謂非恩。

translations.literal: Gao answered: "The Chen ruler formerly at our court — not because he admired righteousness and came; the sovereign granted him pillar state, rank reaching human ministers; sons, daughters, jade, silk — full rites were about to send; thereupon he held the altars of soil and grain — who says it was not grace.
translations.idiomatic: Du Gao replied, "Your emperor was once at our court not because he sought virtue but because we raised him — we made him a pillar state, gave him every honor, even prepared sons and daughters, jade and silk to send with him when he took the throne. Is that not kindness?

sentences.zh: 郝烈之徒，邊民狂狡，曾未報德，而先納之。

translations.literal: Hao Lie and his sort, frontier people wild and cunning, had never repaid grace, yet were first received.
translations.idiomatic: As for Hao Lie and men like him — unruly border folk who had never repaid Zhou's kindness — you took them in first.

sentences.zh: 今受華氏，正是相報。

translations.literal: Now receiving the Hua clan — precisely is mutual repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Our accepting Hua Jiao is simply returning the favor.

sentences.zh: 過自彼始，豈在本朝。

translations.literal: Fault from that state begins; how could it be at our court.
translations.idiomatic: The offense began on your side, not ours.

sentences.zh: 」陵曰：「彼納華皎，志圖吞噬。

translations.literal: " Ling said: "That court receiving Hua Jiao — intent and plan to swallow and devour.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Ling said, "Your court took in Hua Jiao because you mean to swallow our territory.

sentences.zh: 此受郝烈，容之而已。

translations.literal: This receiving Hao Lie — merely accommodating them, that's all.
translations.idiomatic: You took Hao Lie only to give him shelter.

sentences.zh: 且華皎方州列將，竊邑叛亡。

translations.literal: Moreover Hua Jiao was a provincial-column general; stealthily holding a walled town, rebel and flee.
translations.idiomatic: And Hua Jiao was a provincial commander who seized a district and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 郝烈一百許戶，脫身逃竄。

translations.literal: Hao Lie about a hundred-odd households; stripped body and fled in stealth.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Lie is a mere hundred or so households who slipped away.

sentences.zh: 大小有異，豈得同年而語乎？

translations.literal: Large and small have difference; how can they be spoken of in the same year!
translations.idiomatic: Surely the two cases are not comparable?

sentences.zh: 」杲曰：「大小雖殊，受降一也。

translations.literal: " Gao said: "Large and small though different, receiving surrender is one.
translations.idiomatic: " Du Gao said, "Different in scale, perhaps — but accepting defection is the same thing.

sentences.zh: 若論先後，本朝無失。

translations.literal: If discussing before and after, our court has no fault.
translations.idiomatic: And as for who acted first, our court is not in the wrong.

sentences.zh: 」陵曰：「周朝送主上還國，旣以為恩；

translations.literal: " Ling said: "The Zhou court sent the sovereign back to his state — already taking this as grace;
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Ling replied, "Zhou sent our emperor home — that you call a kindness;

sentences.zh: 衛公共元定渡江，敦云非怨。

translations.literal: Duke of Wei together with Yuan Ding crossed the river — sincerely saying it is not resentment.
translations.idiomatic: yet Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi crossed the Yangzi with Yuan Ding — and you insist there was no ill will.

sentences.zh: 計恩之與怨，亦足相埒。

translations.literal: Calculating grace and resentment — also sufficient to be equal and comparable.
translations.idiomatic: By that reckoning, favor and grievance seem about evenly matched.

sentences.zh: 」杲曰：「元定等兵敗身囚，其怨已滅。

translations.literal: " Gao said: "Yuan Ding and the others were defeated in battle and taken prisoner; their grievance is already extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Du Gao replied that Yuan Ding and his men had been defeated and captured, so any score against them was already settled.

sentences.zh: 陳主負扆馮玉，其恩猶在。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler sits with back to the screen leaning on jade; his favor still remains.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor still sits on his throne, and the debt of gratitude to Zhou has not vanished.

sentences.zh: 且怨繇彼國，恩起本朝，以怨酬恩，未之聞也。

translations.literal: Moreover the grievance arose from that state, the favor arose from our dynasty; using grievance to repay favor — never heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the wrong came from Chen, while the favor came from our court — to answer kindness with resentment is something I have never heard of.

sentences.zh: 」陵乃笑而不答。

translations.literal: " Ling laughed and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: At that Xu Ling laughed and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 杲因謂之曰：「今三方鼎立，各圖進取，苟有釁隙，實啟敵心。

translations.literal: Gao then said to him: "Now the three sides stand as a tripod, each plotting advance; if there is any breach, it truly opens the enemy's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Du Gao went on: "The three powers now stand in balance, each seeking advantage; the smallest rift would only hearten our common foe.

sentences.zh: 本朝與陳，日敦鄰睦，輶軒往返，積有歲年。

translations.literal: Our dynasty and Chen daily cultivate neighborly friendship; diplomatic carriages go back and forth, accumulating for years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Chen have cultivated neighborly ties for years, with envoys passing constantly between us.

sentences.zh: 比為疆埸之事，遂為仇敵，構怨連兵，略無寧歲，鷸蚌狗兔，勢不俱全。

translations.literal: Recently because of frontier affairs they became enemies, building grievances and continuous warfare, hardly a peaceful year; snipe and clam, dog and hare — the situation cannot have all survive.
translations.idiomatic: Recently border troubles turned us into enemies, grievance piled upon arms, and scarcely a year has passed in peace — like the snipe and the clam or the dog and the hare, both sides cannot come out whole.

sentences.zh: 若使齊寇乘之，則彼此危矣。

translations.literal: If Qi invaders take advantage, then both sides are in peril.
translations.idiomatic: If Northern Qi seizes the moment, both our states will be in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 孰與心忿悔禍，遷慮改圖，陳國息爭桑之心，本朝弘灌瓜之義，張旃拭玉，脩好如初，共為掎角，以取齊氏。

translations.literal: Which is better: in heart resent and repent the calamity, shift thought and change plan; Chen ceases the heart of fighting over mulberry, our dynasty expands the meaning of watering melons; spread banners and wipe jade, restore friendship as before, jointly form pincers to take the Qi house.
translations.idiomatic: Would it not be better to turn from anger, reconsider the harm, and change course — for Chen to set aside border quarrels, for Zhou to uphold neighborly generosity, to renew friendship as before and act in concert against Qi?

sentences.zh: 非唯兩主之慶，實亦兆庶賴之。

translations.literal: Not only the joy of the two rulers, but truly also the multitude relies on it.
translations.idiomatic: That would bring joy not only to both sovereigns, but relief to all our peoples.

sentences.zh: 」陵具以聞，陳宣帝許之。

translations.literal: " Ling reported in full; Emperor Xuandi of Chen agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling reported everything to the throne, and Emperor Xuandi of Chen assented.

sentences.zh: 遂遣使來聘。

translations.literal: Then envoys were sent on a friendly visit.
translations.idiomatic: Chen then dispatched envoys on a goodwill mission.

sentences.zh: 武帝建德初，為司城中大夫，使於陳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jian'ede of Emperor Wu, he was made chief minister of the city quarter and sent as envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiande era under Emperor Wu, Du Gao was appointed chief minister of the city quarter and again sent as envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳宣帝謂杲曰：「長湖公軍人等雖築館處之，然恐不能無北風之戀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuandi of Chen said to Gao: "Although Changhu Duke's military men and others are housed in built quarters, I fear there cannot but be longing for the north wind.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuandi of Chen told Du Gao: "Though Changhu Duke's soldiers are lodged comfortably, I suppose they must still long for the north.

sentences.zh: 王褒、庾信之徒旣羈旅關中，亦當有南枝之思耳。

translations.literal: Wang Bao, Yu Xin and the like, being detained travelers in Guanzhong, should also have thoughts of the southern branch.
translations.idiomatic: And Wang Bao, Yu Xin, and others held in Guanzhong must surely miss the south as well.

sentences.zh: 」杲揣陳宣意，欲以元定軍將士易王褒等。

translations.literal: Gao gauged Emperor Xuandi of Chen's intent: he wanted to exchange Yuan Ding's army officers and soldiers for Wang Bao and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Du Gao perceived that the emperor meant to trade Yuan Ding's captured officers and men for Wang Bao and his fellow émigrés.

sentences.zh: 乃答之曰：「長湖總戎失律，臨難苟免，旣不死節，安用以為。

translations.literal: He answered: "Changhu commanded the army but violated discipline; at crisis saved himself by any means; having not died loyal, what use to make of them.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Changhu failed in command and fled rather than die loyal — what use are such men?

sentences.zh: 且猶牛之一毛，何能損益。

translations.literal: Moreover like one hair of an ox's hide, how can it profit or harm.
translations.idiomatic: They are no more than a single hair from an ox hide — too insignificant to matter.

sentences.zh: 本朝之議，初未及此。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's deliberations initially had not reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Our court never considered such an exchange in the first place.

sentences.zh: 」陳宣帝乃止，杲還至石頭，又遣謂之曰：「若欲合從，共圖齊氏，能以樊、鄧見與，方可表信。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuandi of Chen then stopped; when Gao returned to Shitou, Chen again sent someone saying: "If you wish horizontal alliance jointly to plot Qi, if you can give Fan and Deng in visible transfer, then you can show good faith.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor dropped the matter. When Du Gao reached Shitou on his return, Chen sent word again: "If you truly want an alliance against Qi, you must cede Fan and Deng to prove your sincerity.

sentences.zh: 」杲答曰：「合從圖齊，豈唯弊邑之利。

translations.literal: " Gao answered: "Horizontal alliance to plot Qi — is it only my humble state's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: " Du Gao replied: "An alliance against Qi would benefit Chen no less than Zhou.

sentences.zh: 必須城鎮，宜待之於齊。

translations.literal: If towns and fortresses are required, they should be awaited from Qi.
translations.idiomatic: If you want strongholds, wait until we take them from Qi.

sentences.zh: 先索漢南，使者不敢聞命。

translations.literal: To demand Han-nan first — the envoy dares not hear the command.
translations.idiomatic: To demand Han-nan up front — your envoy cannot accept such terms.

sentences.zh: 」還，除司倉中大夫。

translations.literal: " On return he was appointed chief minister of granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home, Du Gao was appointed chief minister of granaries.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：韋、辛、皇甫之徒，並關右之舊族也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Wei, Xin, Huangfu and the like were all old clans of Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Wei, Xin, Huangfu, and men like them were all established families of Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 或紆組登朝，獲當官之譽；

translations.literal: Some wore the official sash and ascended court, gaining praise fitting their office;
translations.idiomatic: Some entered court in official rank and won praise for how they held their posts;

sentences.zh: 或張旃出境，有專對之才。

translations.literal: Some spread banners going abroad, having talent for independent repartee.
translations.idiomatic: Others went abroad as envoys and showed a gift for holding their own in diplomacy.

sentences.zh: 旣茂國猷，克隆家業。

translations.literal: They enriched state plans, and perpetuated family enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: They served the state ably and carried on their families' good names.

sentences.zh: 美矣夫！

translations.literal: How beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Truly admirable!

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou (November 1971).
